Discrepancy

/dih-SKREP-uhn-see/ - the stress falls on SKREP · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Discrepancy means a mismatch between things that should correspond — a gap that might still be explained or squared.

The moving company's invoice listed eleven boxes; Dana's photos showed nine - a discrepancy she circled twice in red.

Worked Example

Applying for her first passport, Suki hit a discrepancy: her birth certificate said March 2, her hospital bracelet March 3. Some clerk, sixty years ago, had slipped by a day - and until the two records agreed, the application sat in a drawer.

Discrepancy is the precise word because two official records of one fact refuse to agree. The word passes no judgment - it does not say which paper is wrong or accuse anyone of lying. It just names the gap, and gaps in records must be explained before anything built on them can proceed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

mismatch: the plain word for two things failing to line up

inconsistency: statements or behavior that don't hold together

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

agreement: the two records tell one story

alignment: point-for-point matching between accounts

Where it sits · how hard the two are to reconcile — variation → discrepancy → contradiction

variation vs. discrepancy: Variation is the everyday wiggle between two honest readings; a discrepancy goes further - a gap wide enough to demand an explanation.

contradiction vs. discrepancy: Contradiction outranks discrepancy: two figures with a discrepancy might yet be squared, but two accounts in contradiction can never both be true.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart

Root — crep

Root — crep: to rattle, creak

Suffix — -ancy

Suffix — -ancy: state of

Put it together

Put it together: Dis- (apart) + crep (to rattle, creak) + -ancy (state of) = the state of rattling apart. Latin discrepare meant 'to sound out of tune': two ledgers with a discrepancy are two instruments playing different notes where there should be one sound.

Use the root in a new word: decrepit

Use the root in a new word: decrepit: The decrepit pier creaked and rattled under every footstep.

Word Choice

neutral / formal

A discrepancy lives between two records that should match and don't - ledgers, counts, clocks. It is a fact to explain, not an accusation. Keep it apart from ambiguity, this unit's two-readings word: ambiguity is one text read two ways; a discrepancy is two accounts of one fact.
